text: FOREWORD This is the second of the major studies sponsored by the Office of Population Research to deal primarily with India.
text_raw:
FOREWORD 
This is the second of the major studies sponsored by the Office of 
Population Research to deal primarily with India.

text: Its predecessor, that by Kingsley Davis entitled The Population of India and Pakistan, was a general analysis of the demographic position with special emphasis on the sociological aspects of the problem.
text_raw:
Its predecessor, 
that by Kingsley Davis entitled The Population of India and 
Pakistan, was a general analysis of the demographic position with 
special emphasis on the sociological aspects of the problem.

text: This work by Coale and Hoover differs from that by Davis in three important particulars.
text_raw:
This 
work by Coale and Hoover differs from that by Davis in three 
important particulars.

text: In the first place, it is directed to economic problems.
text_raw:
In the first place, it is directed to economic 
problems.

text: In the second place, it is a sharply focused attempt to give as concrete an answer as possible to a specific question, namely:
text_raw:
In the second place, it is a sharply focused attempt to 
give as concrete an answer as possible to a specific question, namely:

text: What difference would it make in economic terms if the birth rate, instead of remaining unchanged, should be cut drastically in this generation?
text_raw:
What difference would it make in economic terms if the birth rate, 
instead of remaining unchanged, should be cut drastically in this 
generation?

text: Finally, although the book deals mainly with India, it is directed toward the more general situation of the underdevelÂ¬ oped countries.
text_raw:
Finally, although the book deals mainly with India, 
it is directed toward the more general situation of the underdevelÂ¬ 
oped countries.

text: India is in effect the principal example, but in the latter part of the work the position is reviewed to determine the extent to which the major conclusions drawn for India are valid for other low-income countries, including those with less densely settled populations.
text_raw:
India is in effect the principal example, but in the 
latter part of the work the position is reviewed to determine the 
extent to which the major conclusions drawn for India are valid 
for other low-income countries, including those with less densely 
settled populations.

text: Here the major illustration is Mexico, where several aspects of the situation contrast rather sharply with those of India.
text_raw:
Here the major illustration is Mexico, where 
several aspects of the situation contrast rather sharply with those 
of India.

text: Throughout, the authors have endeavored to make their analysis highly specific and to carry it out in quantitative terms as far as possible.
text_raw:
Throughout, the authors have endeavored to make their analysis 
highly specific and to carry it out in quantitative terms as far as 
possible.

text: Indeed, it is in the exploration of dynamic numerical models for both the economy and the population that this work contrasts most sharply with other attempts to evaluate economic consequences of alternative trends in human fertility.
text_raw:
Indeed, it is in the exploration of dynamic numerical 
models for both the economy and the population that this work 
contrasts most sharply with other attempts to evaluate economic 
consequences of alternative trends in human fertility.

The basic method used in projecting the Mexican population was the

text: The ingredients required for making such a projection were the same: a base population for a recent year given by sex and five-year age groups; current mortality rates by age and sex; current fertility rates by age of mother; and proÂ¬ jected mortality and fertility rates.

text: However, the techniques employed in assembling these necessary ingredients were considerably less elaboÂ¬ rate than those used for India.

text: The methods used were simpler because of the greater completeness of Mexican population data, particularly vital statistics; because an especially useful set of model life tables was published by the United Nations since the Indian projections were completed; and because of a recognition that some of the refined adjustments applied to Indian population data were unnecessary in that they made little difference to the economic analysis.

recognition that some of the refined adjustments applied to Indian 
population data were unnecessary in that they made little difference to 
the economic analysis.

text: And, secondly, there is a body of widely cited evidence indicating a substantial rural- urban differential in fertility already existing in Mexico.2 The evidence most often cited is the higher ratio of children 0-4 to women 15-49 in areas having a higher proportion of their population rural.

text: Though there is little doubt of some sort of fertility differential (with higher rural than urban rates), the data available are not adequate for estimating how large the differential is, or even for being certain that the risks of childbearing for an urban resident are intrinsically lower than for a rural resident.

text: All of this reasoning is very tenuous and it can be used to support only a very tentative conclusion: namely, that it remains uncertain what part of rural-urban differences in Mexican fertility are due to basically different risks of childbearing in the urban environment, and what part are transitory effects due to the selective migration of less fertile persons.
text_raw:
All of this reasoning is very tenuous and it can be used to support only 
a very tentative conclusion: namely, that it remains uncertain what part 
of rural-urban differences in Mexican fertility are due to basically 
different risks of childbearing in the urban environment, and what part 
are transitory effects due to the selective migration of less fertile persons.

text: If the second cause accounts for most of the differences between rural and urban fertility the implication is that further increases in urbanizaÂ¬ tion could not be expected to have much effect on the all-Mexico level of births.
text_raw:
If the second cause accounts for most of the differences between rural 
and urban fertility the implication is that further increases in urbanizaÂ¬ 
tion could not be expected to have much effect on the all-Mexico level 
of births.

text: On the other hand if the difference between rural and urban fertility is large, and it reflects a fundamental difference in the risks of childbearing in the rural and urban environments, then the expected continuation of increasing urbanism could be expected on its own to effect a measurable reduction in the Mexican birth rate.
text_raw:
On the other hand if the difference between rural and urban 
fertility is large, and it reflects a fundamental difference in the risks of 
childbearing in the rural and urban environments, then the expected 
continuation of increasing urbanism could be expected on its own to 
effect a measurable reduction in the Mexican birth rate.

text: The likely course of mortality and fertility in Mexico during the next 30 years can be stated with considerable brevity, if not confidence or precision.

30 years can be stated with considerable brevity, if not confidence or 
precision.

text: Death rates, having fallen very extensively during the last 25 years, will continue to drop.
text_raw:
Death rates, having fallen very extensively during the last 
25 years, will continue to drop.

text: Fertility will probably continue at least for a few years at the apparently unchanging level characteristic of its recent history.
text_raw:
Fertility will probably continue at least 
for a few years at the apparently unchanging level characteristic of its 
recent history.

text: There is some possibility of a decline beginning in a few years as a consequence of the social and economic changes accomÂ¬ panying continued industrialization and urbanization.
text_raw:
There is some possibility of a decline beginning in a few 
years as a consequence of the social and economic changes accomÂ¬ 
panying continued industrialization and urbanization.

text: The basis for believing that such a decline will occur cannot be established without a better understanding than now available of the existence, extent, and circumstances of rural-urban and other differences in Mexican fertility levels.
text_raw:
The basis for 
believing that such a decline will occur cannot be established without 
a better understanding than now available of the existence, extent, and 
circumstances of rural-urban and other differences in Mexican fertility 
levels.

text: There is little doubt that an acceleration in the spread of educaÂ¬ tion as well as a continuation of urbanization and industrialization would provide a more receptive environment for the spread of the small-family custom.
text_raw:
There is little doubt that an acceleration in the spread of educaÂ¬ 
tion as well as a continuation of urbanization and industrialization would 
provide a more receptive environment for the spread of the small-family
